posts.author: Galv
posts.body:
Layer Graphics
RPG Maker MZ Plugin
Galv
​
Introduction
I couldn't live without graphic layers. Ported this one from my MV Plugin.
Features
This plugin allows you to use graphics as layers on the map, designed to be used for layer mapping (parallax mapping), fogs and other effects.
Layers can move at different speed to player movement (useful for perspective effects), slide like fogs, display at different levels on the map (below map, below characters, above everything, etc.), opacity, blend, etc.
Uses 'Plugin' command to change layer settings during game.
Can also create layers for battles.
How to Use
- Copy the "GALV_LayerGraphicsMZ.js" file into your project's /js/plugins/ folder.
- Activate plugin using the 'Plugin Manager'
- Create a new folder in your project: /img/layers/
- Use Plugin commands to setup layers
- Read the 'HELP' documentation (also found in plugin manager) for more details and try the demo if you don't understand.
Plugin
Get it here
Credit and Thanks
- Galv
Terms
Free to use in any RPG Maker MZ project including commercial. Please credit "Galv".

0 0 255 5 10 0 0 vs 0 0 255 0.5 10 0 0 ?
Thank you!
Click to expand...
As rpgLord69 said, please look at the documentation. Each of those numbers align with the words below:
LAYER ID GRAPHIC XSPEED YSPEED OPACITY Z XSHIFT YSHIFT BLEND
LAYER_S ID GRAPHIC X Y OPACITY Z BLEND XANCHOR YANCHOR CHARACTER ROTATE

Question: does this work on maps that are quite big?
I've used this for a while now and I have problems when a map goes above a certain size.
I'm currently trying to apply a shadow-map to an 80x100 map but it doesn't work.
Previously it wouldn't work on a 64x50 map, but I managed to get it fixed in the end.
But is there such a thing as too big for this plugin?

posts.author: Galv
posts.body:
I have not tried that large, but doing a quick search it seems dependent on computer with a max of 4096x4096px seemingly widely supported.
Instead of doing one large shadow map, you could create a few smaller ones using the static layer and positioning them in the correct positions on the map.
